promises.label: Additional $20 billion share repurchases
promises.commitment: Authorize an additional $20 billion in share repurchases; described as a multiyear plan with activity each quarter, without a fixed end date.
promises.outcomeSummary: The authorization remained open; Q3 repurchases were $750 million, diluted share count declined ~3% YoY, and roughly $15 billion remained.

missing.what_was_said: Management described the authorization as a multiyear plan, said it would be active every quarter, and committed at least half of cash-flow generation over the coming years to share repurchases.
Uber repurchased a record $3 billion in Q1, contributing to a 2% YoY reduction in diluted share count. It retired approximately 40 million shares, versus roughly 80 million during all of 2025.

Q2 repurchases were $510 million while approximately $4 billion was invested in Delivery Hero. Management explained that it had tactically pivoted toward M&A and expected to rebuild repurchase levels in 'months, not quarters.' This changed execution pace, not the $20 billion authorization.

missing.what_was_said: Management described insurance reform and product-driven “hundreds of millions of dollars of cost savings that we are seeing” as providing leverage to hold prices “flat or better in certain markets.” This was stronger evidence of progress than the prepared-remarks outlook alone.

Management explicitly reiterated that it expected hundreds of millions of dollars of insurance savings “this year.” It also reported that price reductions had already translated into accelerating trip growth, distinguishing realized customer benefits from the still-projected annual savings amount.
